svg.text: Repaso — the agent fleet, audited
Thirteen agents. Every one of them is paired with a green deterministic function that owns the number the agent is not allowed to invent.
13 agents · 4 graph builders · 1 harness
8 call Bedrock · 5 carry no model at all
100 % Amazon Bedrock — no other provider
AGENT
WHAT IT DECIDES
MODEL TIER
THE DETERMINISTIC COUNTERPART — what owns the math
WHAT IT CAN REFUSE
INGEST
SESSION
RESPONSE
DAILY CLOSE
Intake Screener
ingest · node screen
Whether a photographed worksheet is safe to put in
front of a model at all.
Nova Lite · classify
after a deterministic pass
tools.guardrails.Screener — a deny-list over canonicalised text (case, accents and
whitespace folded), plus email / national-id / phone redaction before any prompt.
It runs BEFORE the model, and a model error is never read as "safe" — the verdict
returns unsafe. The Armor fails closed by construction.
Quarantines the material with an EvidenceSpan
quoting the payload. 400/400 adversarial payloads
intercepted, 9 families, ES + EN, OCR-corrupted
included; 0 % false block on 200 clean texts.
Material Parser
ingest · node parse
Whether the photo is legible enough to build items
from, and what the text on it actually says.
no model — deterministic
core.harness.legibility — Laplacian blur variance and contrast standard deviation,
combined with the OCR confidence by effective_confidence() and compared against
the blur floor of 300. Textract supplies characters; the judgement is arithmetic.
Asks for a re-photo rather than guessing at a
smudged digit. An unparsed page ends the graph
before a single model call is paid for.
Competency Mapper
ingest · node map
Which curriculum competency this material is
teaching.
Haiku 4.5 · structured
The knowledge retriever proposes the candidate set; _keep_known() drops any id the
model returned that the taxonomy did not offer, and de-duplicates the rest. If the
call fails, the retriever's own confidence ranking is used instead.
No candidate above the retrieval floor means the
material is politely rejected. It cannot invent a
competency the taxonomy does not contain.
Item Generator
ingest · node generate
The six practice items drafted from this material.
Sonnet 4.6 · generate
holds a stage claim
is_valid_draft() structural validation — stem, options and answer key present and
mutually consistent — plus a Provenance stamp carrying prompt version, model id
and source. The stage claim is why a crash resumes instead of regenerating.
A draft that fails structure never becomes an item.
Zero surviving drafts ends the graph with a request
for one worked example, not with a guess.
Item Critic
ingest · node validate
Whether each drafted item is correct, on-grade and
unambiguous.
Sonnet 4.6 · judge
map_flaws() forces free prose into a typed ItemFlaw enum, and the accept / reject
status is written by code from that verdict. The critic's paragraph is never what
changes an item's status in the store.
Rejects an item outright. If every item in a batch
is rejected, the material itself is refused rather
than half-published.
Answerability Probe
ingest · node validate
Whether the item can be answered without ever seeing
the material it came from.
Nova Micro · probe
combine(verdict, answered_blind): accepted becomes verdict.accepted AND
answered_blind is not True. A blind-answerable item is force-rejected and flagged
ANSWERABLE_WITHOUT_MATERIAL even when the critic approved it.
Kills an item that measures nothing — the one veto
in the fleet that overrides another model's
approval, and it is arithmetic that applies it.
Session Planner
session · node plan
Which items a child practises today, and in what
order.
no model — deterministic
core.harness.sm2.due_items() over the SpacedItemState rows, with one slot reserved
for an item the student has never seen. An EXAM# date inside 7 days caps the
capsule at 4 and re-sorts it weakest-EMA first.
Nothing due means no session and no message that
day: silence is a legal output. A second run on the
same date exits idempotently.
Capsule Composer
session · node compose
The framing words wrapped around today's items.
Sonnet 4.6 · generate
render_item() and item_buttons() render the question text and the answer buttons
from the stored Item. The composer's output is concatenated around them and never
replaces them, so a hallucinated option cannot reach a child.
It has no refusal — and no power either: it cannot
change a question, an option or an answer key.
It only chooses the greeting.
Grader
response · node grade
Whether an open answer is correct, and on what
evidence.
Sonnet 4.6 · judge
MCQ never reaches a model
grade_mcq() is exact matching in code. For open answers the confidence gate is 0.85
and an EvidenceSpan quoting the child is mandatory; the text sent to Bedrock is the
redacted copy, never the raw reply.
Below 0.85 the grade does not exist: correct is None,
mastery and SM-2 are left untouched, and the answer
is handed to the parent to settle.
Adaptation Policy
response · node adapt
Continue, raise or lower difficulty, switch to open
answers, reduce the load.
Haiku 4.5 · structured
core.harness.escalation_triggers — struggle_trigger (9 attempts of evidence, 7-day
cooldown), engagement_trigger and fast_guess_flag. fallback_decision() is computed
first, and is what is returned whenever a trigger fired or the model call failed.
It cannot veto an interrupt and it cannot
manufacture one. When a trigger fires, the model's
reply is discarded unread.
Escalation Composer
response · escalate — close · cohort
How to word the message that interrupts a parent,
and which triage options it offers.
Sonnet 4.6 · generate
engagement notes: template
The triggers decide IF; triage_options() fixes the reply buttons; evidence_digest()
carries the quoted spans through unchanged. The cohort note is drafted from a k ≥ 3
aggregate whose prompt never receives an alias or a name.
It never decides whether to interrupt — only how to
say it. The 7-day per-student cooldown is enforced
upstream, out of its reach.
Goal Verifier
close · node verify
Whether today actually closed: every response
graded, every quarantine and escalation accounted for.
no model — deterministic
verify_daily() reconciles sessions, grades, quarantines and escalations into a
DailyCloseReport, and BoundedAttempts(2) caps the rework it may request.
Refuses to loop. After two attempts an unresolved
item is reported as unresolved rather than retried
until it costs money.
Item Lifecycle Optimizer
close · node optimize
Which items leave the bank.
no model — deterministic
core.harness.psychometrics.should_retire() — point-biserial discrimination below
0.15, or a p-value outside 0.05–0.95, with at least 8 observed attempts.
The statistic retires the item; nothing else in the system can.
Retires an item on its own statistics. No model
gets a vote on what stays in the bank.
Why the green column is the point of this diagram
Spacing intervals, mastery, escalation thresholds and item statistics are not opinions a model produced — they are functions with unit tests, and the fleet is wired so that no agent
can overrule them. Read that column and you have read the pedagogy. Offline, the whole Bedrock column is replaced by LocalPlaybackModel, a strict playback double that raises on
any unplanned call — which is why 706 tests run in ~5 s with zero credentials and zero network, and why the suite doubles as a cost audit.
Model ids pinned in config/models.py with a per-role fallback chain on throttle. Numbers from calibration-validation 2026-08-20 · armor-bench 2026-08-20 · calendar-gaps 2026-08-21.
